recognize_zh: 三顆受感染紅血球整個被寄生蟲占滿，內有分散的棕褐色瘧色素與粉紅/紅紫色染色質團，上方兩顆各有一個偏心的染色質塊，符合間日瘧（P. vivax）配子體；下方那顆有兩點染色質，也可能是早期裂殖體。
features: Infected red cells nearly filled by a single rounded parasite, at least as large as uninfected red cells
Abundant scattered fine golden-brown hemozoin pigment throughout the parasite
Single compact eccentric magenta chromatin mass in two parasites (gametocyte pattern)
One parasite with two chromatin dots, possibly an early schizont rather than a gametocyte
Schuffner stippling and red cell enlargement not clearly assessable at this resolution; no ring forms or banana-shaped gametocytes
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows scattered red cells occupied by large rounded parasites that fill most of the host cell and contain diffusely scattered brown hemozoin pigment. Two parasites have a single compact eccentric chromatin mass, consistent with gametocytes, while a third has two chromatin dots and may represent an early schizont. Crescent-shaped gametocytes and multiple fine ring forms are not seen, although Schuffner stippling and host cell enlargement are difficult to assess at this magnification. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium vivax infection with circulating gametocytes; parasitemia quantification and confirmatory PCR or antigen testing are recommended.

ddx.vs: P. ovale also produces round gametocytes with Schuffner dots, but infected cells are often oval with fimbriated edges and the parasite is more compact with coarser pigment; PCR distinguishes them reliably.
P. malariae gametocytes occur in normal-sized or smaller red cells without stippling and with coarse dark pigment, alongside band-form trophozoites.
P. falciparum gametocytes are crescent or banana shaped, and trophozoites/schizonts are rarely seen in peripheral blood.
Babesia forms small rings and tetrads without hemozoin pigment and without large gametocytes.
